text: This lesson writes the real CREATE TABLE statement for dw.FactProductSales, the fact table at the center of this warehouse.

Notice the four key columns — ProductKey, OrderDateKey, TerritoryKey, CustomerKey — are plain integers with no REFERENCES constraint. That's deliberate: the dimension tables they'll point at don't exist yet. SQL Server would reject a foreign key against a table that isn't built.

Every column here falls into one of three groups: surrogate foreign keys that will resolve to a dimension's key, degenerate dimensions like SalesOrderID that identify the source row directly, and measures like OrderQty and LineTotal that every report ultimately aggregates.
Next lesson builds and populates all four dimension tables this fact table will reference — DimProduct, DimDate, DimTerritory, and DimCustomer.
